title: A Survey of Token Compression for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
version: v5 (01 Feb 2026; formerly When Tokens Talk Too Much)
actual_read_scope: arXiv HTML v5 abstract, introduction, taxonomy/definition, §§2–6 (image/video/audio methods, trade-offs, evaluation/challenges/future directions), application overview, and full reference list; cited original papers were not read.

routes.problem: Spatially dense image patches create redundant multimodal context.
routes.mechanism: Pixel unshuffle, pooling/interpolation, or strided convolution reduce a 2D grid before the LLM.
routes.token_connection: Direct physical reduction N→M; usually fixed ratios (often 25% retained), with locality preserved.

routes.problem: Neighboring or semantically similar visual tokens duplicate information.
routes.mechanism: Similarity clustering, bipartite merging, or diversity-aware selection merges/selects representative patches.
routes.token_connection: Direct N→M; may lose spatial detail and fine-grained distinctions.

routes.problem: Many visual tokens receive little attention after early layers.
routes.mechanism: Use encoder or decoder attention to prune low-saliency tokens, sometimes progressively by layer.
routes.token_connection: Direct N→M and usually training-free/post-training; attention-score computation and kernel compatibility add deployment caveats.

routes.problem: Only a subset of image content is relevant to the text query.
routes.mechanism: Q-Former/query tokens distill visual content or cross-modal relevance selects patches.
routes.token_connection: Direct and query-conditioned; fixed query length is compact but may require re-condensation in multi-turn use.

routes.problem: Video token counts scale with both frame count and spatial resolution.
routes.mechanism: Frame sampling, temporal clustering, adjacent-token merging, density pruning, and grouped frame compression remove static/spatiotemporal redundancy.
routes.token_connection: Direct input/feature token reduction; temporal compression must preserve motion and rare events.

routes.problem: Long videos contain many frames unrelated to the user query.
routes.mechanism: Cross-modal frame relevance assigns lower compression to salient frames and higher compression elsewhere; Q-former/token distillation is another route.
routes.token_connection: Direct, query-adaptive N→M, with explicit long-video budget control.

routes.problem: High-rate, long-duration audio yields dense temporal/spectral tokens.
routes.mechanism: Token stacking, pooling, and temporal convolution/downsampling (often to 12.5 Hz) reduce sequence length.
routes.token_connection: Direct temporal token reduction; stacking changes hidden dimension and needs an MLP realignment.

routes.problem: Adjacent/spectral audio segments contain redundant or low-saliency information.
routes.mechanism: Adjacent-token cosine merging, top-K spectrogram attention, first-layer decoder attention pruning, and audio-text cross-modal selection.
routes.token_connection: Direct, but silence/noise and contextual cues make aggressive pruning risky.

routes.problem: Variable-length audio needs a compact representation aligned to text.
routes.mechanism: Audio Q-Formers, AV Q-Formers, and learnable queries distill global/local acoustic context to fixed length.
routes.token_connection: Direct fixed-length bottleneck; can combine early audio-visual fusion with query distillation.

routes.problem: Token compression, weight compression, sparse attention, and modality alignment affect different cost axes.
routes.mechanism: Treat token compression as sequence-length N reduction; combine it with quantization/pruning or improved encoders/projectors.
routes.token_connection: Token compression is direct N→M; attention sparsity alone remains N→N and is explicitly out of scope, while weight compression targets D/FLOPs.

candidates.title: An image is worth 1/2 tokens after layer 2: plug-and-play inference acceleration for large vision-language models
candidates.reason: FastV observes very low visual-token attention after early layers and prunes 50% after layer 2 while retaining performance; the survey table provides retained-token/benchmark comparisons.

candidates.title: PruMerge: pruning and merging tokens for efficient vision language models
candidates.reason: Required prior combining visual-token pruning and merging; included as the requested PruMerge lineage and a representative similarity/attention hybrid.

candidates.title: LLaVA-PruMerge: Adaptive token reduction for efficient large multimodal models
candidates.reason: Adaptive visual-token reduction is compared at 144/192/336 retained visual tokens; it is a key requested contemporary PruMerge candidate, with exact survey-table numbers but no arXiv ID in the reference entry.

candidates.title: DyCoke: Dynamic compression of tokens for fast video large language models
candidates.reason: Groups four frames and performs temporal pruning within each group; Table 3 compares 50%/35% retained ratios against FastV and other video methods.

candidates.title: FastVID: Dynamic density pruning for fast video large language models
candidates.reason: Clusters adjacent frame representations and applies DPC-KNN to merge tokens; survey reports 25% and 10% retained-ratio rows, making it a typical temporal redundancy method.

candidates.title: PruneVid: Visual token pruning for efficient video large language models
candidates.reason: Uses frame clustering followed by static-token merging and spatiotemporal consolidation; Table 3 shows performance at 25% and 10% retained ratios.

candidates.title: HoliTom: Holistic token merging for fast video large language models
candidates.reason: Recasts temporal redundancy compression as maximizing compressible redundant features over clustered frames, addressing detail loss from single frame-level representatives; reported at 25%/10% retained ratios.

candidates.title: LongVU: Spatiotemporal adaptive compression for long video-language understanding
candidates.reason: Computes query–frame cross-modal relevance and preserves salient frames with lower compression while enforcing the LLM context budget.

candidates.title: An embarrassingly simple approach for LLM with strong ASR capacity
candidates.reason: Representative audio token stacking route: stacks audio tokens and realigns the changed hidden dimension with an MLP, a concrete audio compression primitive.

candidates.title: Adaptive audio-visual speech recognition via Matryoshka-based multimodal LLMs
candidates.reason: Uses multi-scale audio/video training with pooling or stacking at different rates, enabling inference-time compression/performance trade-offs within one model.

candidates.title: Token pruning in audio transformers: optimizing performance and decoding patch importance
candidates.reason: Top-K selection inside audio spectrogram transformer blocks retains tokens ranked by attention magnitude, directly targeting audio-token sequence length.

candidates.title: SpeechPrune: Context-aware token pruning for speech information retrieval
candidates.reason: Uses first-layer decoder attention and audio–text cosine similarity to discard less relevant audio tokens, connecting attention pruning with query-guided selection.

gaps/conflicts: The survey’s strict inclusion rule is physical sequence reduction M<N; attention sparsity that preserves N is excluded even if it lowers FLOPs. Keep this boundary when mapping architecture proposals.

Image/video/audio are the primary axes and transformation/similarity/attention/query the mechanism axes, but several methods combine axes (e.g., query relevance plus clustering, or early fusion plus Q-Former). Assign a primary route and retain cross-links.

Compression ratios and benchmark scores are not a universal performance–token curve: tables mix models, retained-ratio definitions, datasets, and evaluation protocols. A lower ratio can preserve aggregate scores while losing rare spatial, temporal, or acoustic details.

Video compression has a rare-event and motion risk: frame sampling, clustering, or static-token merging may discard short events; query-guided methods depend on the quality of cross-modal relevance and context-budget allocation.
Audio has distinctive spectral/temporal redundancy, silence, and noise. Aggressive pruning can remove contextual cues; the survey identifies principled audio-token pruning as an open challenge.
Weight quantization/pruning and sparse attention are complementary efficiency mechanisms, not token compression under the survey’s definition. Report them separately from N→M token reduction.
The v5 revision is dated 2026-02-01. The reference list includes works through 2025 and the survey’s own 2026 revision; it does not establish coverage of papers released after that date.
